A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CQN-AS research. The main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching the relocated HumanoidBench material.

before.justification: V5 reports original CQN-AS simulation results on BiGym, RLBench and HumanoidBench, alongside motivating experiments and ablations.

after.justification: V6 retains these original results and adds no-op action experiments, a Point-mass study and a preliminary offline RL comparison.

M1.justification: The core critic architecture, objectives and inference procedure remain unchanged. Appendix D newly reports a CQN-AS adaptation combined with Cal-QL and a trial using a ResNet-18 encoder, constituting limited method variants.

E1.justification: V6 adds a 2D Point-mass reaching task and an offline-only evaluation on the existing Sandwich Remove task. The original BiGym, RLBench, HumanoidBench and torque-control task coverage remains; HumanoidBench's relocation does not constitute new coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix D introduces CQN + Cal-QL as the comparator for CQN-AS + Cal-QL. The established BiGym/RLBench comparators CQN, DrQ-v2+ and ACT, and HumanoidBench comparators CQN and SAC, are retained.

E3.justification: V6 extends the sequence-length sweep to 32 and adds controls with 0, 54, 144 and 294 no-op action dimensions. New protocols compare eight single-step actions against five-step Bezier sequences in Point-mass and use 26 successful plus 10 failed trajectories for offline RL. Main benchmark settings in Tables 1-4 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new no-op dimensionality controls and raw-action versus sequence-action DQN study substantially expand analysis of the central methodological motivation. V6 also extends the length ablation to 32 and reports the computational obstacle encountered with ResNet-18. Existing RL-objective, N-step, temporal-ensemble and torque-control analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 9 newly specifies ten runs for Point-mass. Run counts and confidence-interval reporting in retained figures remain unchanged; there is no established increase in their runs. The new offline results include ± uncertainties without defining their statistical meaning.

E6.justification: Primary benchmark curves are unchanged, but existing sequence-length curves are revised: the late-training ordering of lengths 8 and 16 on Saucepan To Hob reverses between v5 Figure 7a and v6 Figure 8a. V6 adds length-32 and toy results, plus offline results of 33 ± 6.8% for CQN-AS + Cal-QL versus 7 ± 14% for CQN + Cal-QL. It removes the standalone stand-return plot and changes the preferred-N statement from {1,3} to {1,4}.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives in Equations (1)-(6), and inference formulation in Appendix C are unchanged. No new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the claims that action sequences benefit value learning and that critic-only CQN-AS avoids actor-driven overestimation and improves benchmark performance. The added analyses support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 now qualifies longer-sequence benefits with plateauing or declining performance when sequences become too long. Appendix D interprets the offline pilot as preliminary evidence of applicability, while Section 6 adds the computational cost of stronger vision encoders as a limitation. Previously documented failure conditions remain elsewhere.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly discloses implementation sources, TD3 exploration standard deviation 0.2 and the no-op wrapper. Appendix D provides offline data composition and a ResNet-18 requirement of at least 48 GB GPU memory. Appendix B adds 13% memory overhead and a 40% slowdown statement while retaining 33%, leaving runtime reporting inconsistent.

R1.justification: V6 adds Nakamoto et al. (2023) for Cal-QL and Kahn et al. (2018) for a proposed future autoregressive, multi-step Q-learning extension. The existing related-work discussion and principal research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The title changes from Robot Learning to Reinforcement Learning. HumanoidBench moves from Appendix A into Section 4.3, and new motivating/preliminary appendices and a NeurIPS checklist appear. Most prose remains intact with localized edits; the checklist contains an unresolved '??' broader-impact reference.

P2.justification: Figure 2 separates SAC and TD3 overestimation panels and replaces the stand-return plot with a no-op table. V6 adds Figure 9, expands the length-ablation legend, relocates the HumanoidBench figure and revises captions and page flow. Most existing displays retain their design.

improvement.justification: V6 modestly strengthens empirical motivation and qualifies longer-sequence benefits through additional controls and the 32-step ablation. New implementation and resource disclosures also help assessment. These gains are tempered by the TD3/SAC mismatch between Figure 2c and Appendix A, conflicting 33%/40% slowdown statements, and unexplained negative 'Distance to Goal' values in Figure 9. The core method and primary benchmark evidence remain stable.
